abstract: We prove that every biplanar graph on at most nineteen vertices is 9-colorable. The new order-nineteen argument combines critical-core extension lemmas with integer-weighted coloring certificates and a complete propositional exclusion. After deleting an independent triple from a hypothetical 10-critical counterexample, earlier extension arguments force a spanning sixteen-vertex 9-critical core. We exclude all 70–72-edge such cores using weighted near-perfect matchings of five explicit exceptional critical graphs. The residual cases have 1,573 augmented-core orbits, checked by exact integer arithmetic and independent labeled coverage. A universal-vertex reduction leaves edge counts 100, 101, and 102. Complete SAT encodings exclude 67, 67, and 68 numerical low-clique profiles, respectively. The difficult saturated cases are reduced by fixing high-to-low nonneighbor sets, with independent coverage checks for 1,420 mask subcases. This representation removes attachment symmetry before the smaller complement graph is searched. A compact supplement reconstructs 1,610 exact final formulas, validates 10,125 actual-coloring axioms, and regenerates independently checkable DRAT refutations. Every computational case has a checked refutation; bounded unsuccessful searches are not used as exclusions. The mathematical dependencies include Gallai's critical-graph theorems, the Kostochka–Stiebitz excess theorem, and Szeider's independence-number-two result. The conclusion raises the minimum possible order of a ten-chromatic biplanar graph to twenty. It neither constructs such a graph nor proves unrestricted 9-colorability.

coauthors.contribution: Eleven- and fifteen-vertex critical-core extension lemmas; the eighteen-vertex coloring exclusion; elementary two-universal-vertex reduction; concurrent universal lifting and small-low-set matching arguments; independent reproduction and scientific audit of the weighted certificates and finite reductions.

title: Weighted coloring extensions and the nineteen-vertex Earth–Moon bound
